newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese Estates sets terms for FRN/loan.
newsitem.headline: Chinese Estates sets terms for FRN/loan.

text.p: A core arranger group has been formed for the US$500 million unsecured financing for Good Top Ltd guaranteed by Chinese Estates Holdings, Citicorp International said Wednesday.

The eight core arrangers are Chase Manhattan Asia, China Development Finance Co HK, Citicorp International, Deutsche Bank Hong Kong branch, Hua Chiao Commercial Bank, Peregrine Fixed Income, American Express Bank and BA Asia.

The financing combines a floating rate note tranche and a term loan/revolving credit tranche. Lenders may participate in the FRN and/or the loan tranches, although those participating in the loan tranche must commit 35 percent to the term loan and 65 percent to the revolving credit.
The facility can be put by the lenders at the end of three years and can be called by Chinese Estates annually.
The interest margin for both the FRN and the loan tranches is set at 165 basis points for years one through three and 190 basis ponts for year four and five.

Proceeds of the five-year facility will refinance existing debt secured against Hong Kong properties Windsor House, Evergo House and Entertainment Building as well as support the group's general corporate funding requirements.
Chinese Estates is rated BBB-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp. An issue-specific rating will be sought for both the FRN and loan tranches.
Citicorp said the deal is believed to be the first in Asia involving a combined FRN/loan financing and the first time a rated syndicated loan will be offered to bank investors in Asia.
The FRNs will be listed on the Luxembourg stock exchange.
